The new superlative
Do you remember? Monza 2024 - Kimi Antonelli
climbed into the Mercedes W15 F1 shortly after his
18th birthday and, as a Friday driver, set lap times
within five laps that left everyone in the pits gaping
in amazement, before he eventually crashed the
car into the tyre barriers. Could a new star have
been rising in the Formula 1 firmament this day?
It is almost inevitable to be reminded of Ayrton
Senna in the Toleman at Monaco in 1984, Michael
Schumacher’s first FL appearance in the Jordan at
Spa-Francorchamps in 1991, or Sebastian Vettel’s
sensational victory at Monza in 2008 in the under-
dog Toro Rosso. All moments that have stuck in
the collective Formula 1 memory.

It may well be that this Andrea Kimi Antonelli com-
mands of the best car on the 2026 grid - but that
has already been the case for many world champi-
ons before him. However, the fact that this super-
cool 20-year-old has crowned himself Formula 1
world champion with three races to go before the
end of the season represents a new superlative.
Following his victory in China, the Italian delivers
his second masterpiece at Suzuka. Although he
drops back to sixth place at the start from pole po-
sition due to spinning wheels, he is back in first
place by the time the safety car is deployed on lap
22. After the restart, the new champion extends
his lead to almost 14 seconds by the finish line.

After many years, the 2026 Monte Carlo Rally fi-
nally lived up to its reputation as an ice and snow
rally once again. Conditions were challenging at
the World Championship opener in the French Ma-
ritime Alps, so it was to be expected that the ex-
perienced rally drivers, in particular, would benefit.
So, it came as a massive surprise that it was none
other than 25-year-old Toyota WRC rookie Oliver
Solberg, co-driven by Elliott Edmondson, who set
the pace right from the start. The young Swede had
already pulled 25 seconds clear of his team-mate
Elfyn Evans by the second special stage and held
on to the overall lead from then until the finish.
The Toyota WRC youngster remained unfazed even
by a puncture, a shattered windscreen and sever-
al skids in the snow, and went on to become the
youngest Monte Carlo winner in WRC history in the
Toyota GR Yaris Rally 1. A sensational debut for the
Toyota Gazoo WRT team. With the top three places,
the Japanese side celebrated a total triumph at the
World Championship opener anyway.
However, the more than two minutes the young
Swede took off his team-mate Ogier’s time at the
finish line was just the beginning of a sensational
season. It was only on the final special stage at
the season finale in Sardinia that Solberg lost the
World Championship title to Elfyn Evans.
